newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes ease Wednesday, talk of deal.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes ease Wednesday, talk of deal.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices edged up late Wednesday, fuelled by a weekly inventory report which showed relatively large draws in crude oil.

West Texas Intermediate cash prices, the basis for West Coast light grades, rose five cents late to $23.20/23.30 a barrel after the American Petroleum Institute reported a 5.7 million barrel draw in crude stocks nationwide last week .
West Coast refinery utilization stood at 88.8 percent, but that remained under normal levels, traders said.
"I think we see it up in the 90s so somebody still is having difficulties," one trader said.

The loss of a fluid catalytic cracker at Mobil's Torrance refinery in California removed 40,000 barrels per day of crude processing from total capacity, but traders said another 75,000 barrels remain unaccounted for.
"I'm looking at who is out trying to move crude, and Chevron (Richmond) is trying to move more than anyone," one trader said.
Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude stayed at $2.05 under WTI October.
Several traders denied a rumor that a cargo of ANS sold for $2.20 a barrel under, adding the price was a bid.
Traders said refineries that normally buy were seen selling Alaska North Slope crude today because they had bought foreign cargoes.
One Northwest refinery offered crude at $2.10 off October WTI, while a Los Angeles refinery sold October ANS at prices based on the monthly average of September.
A major producer of ANS offered the grade at $2.00 under.

Discounts for heavy and light grades could widen on a postings basis because Chevron Corp raised its postings 50 cents late Tuesday, traders said. Other major oil companies announced higher postings late Wednesday.
The rise in postings tracked the early week NYMEX rally.
Values for Kern River rose 30 to 40 cents to $16.40/16.60 cents a gallon on the raised postings.
Wilmington rose 15 cents to $16.25/16.75 a barrel.
Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel, with little trading seen ahead of mid-September.
